body.description: Sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` form fields, not JSON. The Content-Type header value is `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. Validators decode the form body into this object before checking it. The four fields are the page's Step 2 parameters, and all are required. No `redirect_uri` is sent: the page's "redirect_uri is missing" error belongs to the authorization-code exchange on the same endpoint, which is out of scope (no consent flow or consent UI in the product).

refresh_token.description: The programmatic refresh token from the original authorization (`LINKEDIN_REFRESH_TOKEN`). Server-side only; never logged.

client_secret.description: The application's Client Secret (`LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET`). Server-side only; never logged.

body.description: Successful refresh-token exchange. connectors/linkedin/auth.py (TOKEN_URL) calls this surface when LINKEDIN_REFRESH_TOKEN, LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID and LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET are set; a static LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN skips it. VERSIONING: this OAuth endpoint on www.linkedin.com is unversioned. It is the only LinkedIn contract with an absolute URL and without the Linkedin-Version and X-Restli-Protocol-Version headers. `api_version` records the client's pinned 202609 because every contract carries one, not because the endpoint reads it. CACHING: connectors/linkedin/auth.py keeps the access token in memory only, never in the database or logs, and reuses it until `expires_in` minus 300 s after the exchange was sent, then exchanges again; a token whose `expires_in` is at most 300 s is used without being cached. ERRORS: `response.status` lists only 200 because only success bodies are validated against this schema. Errors use the OAuth 2.0 shape {"error": "<code>", "error_description": "<text>"}. The page documents HTTP 400 `invalid_request` with these descriptions: "The provided authorization grant or refresh token is invalid, expired or revoked"; "A required parameter "redirect_uri" is missing"; "A required parameter "grant_type" is missing"; "A required parameter "client_id" is missing"; "A required parameter "refresh_token" is missing". The RFC 6749 section 5.2 codes `invalid_grant`, `invalid_client` and `unauthorized_client` (HTTP 400 or 401) may also occur. CLASSIFICATION, for connectors/linkedin/auth.py and connectors/errors.py: `invalid_grant`, `invalid_client`, `unauthorized_client` and any 401 are AccessDenied, and other 400s are QueryDefect. Exception: LinkedIn reports an expired or revoked refresh token as 400 `invalid_request`, so a 400 whose `error_description` says the grant or token is "invalid, expired or revoked" must be classified as AccessDenied. That switches LinkedIn to simulated data and re-authorization follows the runbook bootstrap; it is not a defect. SCOPES: the sample's `scope` value `r_basicprofile` is the vendor's example; the product's scopes are r_ads, r_ads_reporting and r_marketing_leadgen_automation. SAMPLE: `documented_sample` is the page's Step 2 response copied verbatim. Its token strings are public documentation examples, not credentials.

access_token.description: The new access token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer` on every LinkedIn REST call. About 500 characters; the page advises handling at least 1,000. Held in memory only.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the new access token expires. The page states a 60-day default lifetime; its sample shows 86400.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token, returned with the new access token. The exchange keeps the refresh token's original lifetime, counted from the initial authorization.

refresh_token_expires_in.description: Seconds remaining until the refresh token expires. The exchange does not extend it; once it expires the member must re-authorize the application.

scope.description: Granted member permissions. The page documents a URL-encoded, space-delimited list; consumers split on spaces or commas, so either delimiter parses.
